newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Stocks to suppress Australian GDP - Access.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Stocks to suppress Australian GDP - Access.

text.p: A long-overdue slump in inventory accumulation would suppress Australia's GDP growth over the coming year, Access Economics said on Monday.

"Our view that stockbuilding will ease is the key difference between our forecasts and Treasury's 3.5 percent growth," said the forecaster, predicting 2.9 percent year-average growth in the fiscal year to June 1997.
The Treasury forecast appeared in the August 20 budget and followed 4.1 percent year-average growth recorded in the previous two years.

"Treasury's forecasts on stocks assume that, after three years of producing more than they sold, Australian firms will do so again in 1996/97, to the tune of another A$3 billion," Access said in its quarterly forecasting report. "We think not."
Such strong inventory accumulation had occured before but was always followed by a correction -- a fall in stock levels.
But Treasury forecasts a zero contribution to GDP growth, implying continued inventory accumulation at the same rate as last year.
However, Treasury supported its forecast by saying that the the ratio of stocks to sales seemed to have reached a level that businesses desired.
Access, assuming slower inventory growth, shows stocks detracting 0.5 percentage points from GDP growth in the year.
"Industry data on the composition of stocks suggest the manufacturing sector will be the first to see stock detractions in 1996/97," the consultancy said.
"It will be followed later in 1996/97 by the wholesale sector."
Access economist Chris Richardson said the retail sector might have already begun its stock rundown.
"We may well have already seen part of the rundown in the July retail data, which showed department stores especially clearing their stocks," he told Reuters.
His forecast of a 0.5-percentage-point GDP detraction from all inventories might even be conservative, he added.
"The risk for growth is on the downside."
